note: Fictional demonstration cohort. Every record is a sample; no real award, awardee, or organization is represented. Awardee names are deliberately generic (Organization 1, Company A, Foundation X) so the demonstration carries no bias about awardee types; moku assignments stay specific to show coverage across moku, including cross-moku work. The v0 schema hard-requires sample:true — real data cannot validate against it — and sample TMK cross-references use division digit 9, which no county issues, so no real parcel is referenced.

records.summary: Protects, manages, and restores natural resources in the moku's priority watershed — native forests, plants, and the freshwater that feeds the reef below — through invasive canopy removal, native outplanting, and community stewardship days.

location.geoContext: Riparian parcels along the restoration reach; the working footprint is the stream corridor across both parcels.

records.story: The commitment is the Act 96 commitment: protect, manage, and restore the natural resources the fee exists to care for. Two seasons of workdays replaced invasive canopy with native seedlings grown by a partner nursery, restoring the native forest cover that keeps freshwater in the ground and sediment off the reef. Visitor volunteers join through a stewardship-day signup, putting fee-funded restoration directly in visitors' hands. Survival plots are checked monthly, and every planting day logs its counts before the crew leaves the site.

records.summary: Protects and manages natural resources — intact native forest, plants, and the animals that depend on them — by fencing ungulates out of upland units and tracking native seedling recovery inside the protected area.

location.geoContext: Upland forest management units within a single large parcel; the fence line follows parcel and moku boundaries.

records.story: Five miles of fence line went up across two field seasons, closing the last open corridor into the project's upper units and protecting the native forest, plants, and animals inside. Recovery is measured, not assumed: paired plots inside and outside the fence are surveyed each quarter, and the seedling-survival numbers reported here come from those plots. The crew is hired from within the moku the project serves, and the fence line follows the moku boundary ridge for most of its length.

records.summary: Increases the resilience of community infrastructure — wildfire protection and flood mitigation at the community edge — by converting fallow fire-prone grassland into irrigated greenway firebreaks planted in low-fuel native and food species.

location.geoContext: Fallow parcels mauka of the community edge; the greenway break runs contiguously across both.

records.story: The commitment here is resilience: the roads, homes, and waterlines behind the greenway are the infrastructure the firebreak protects. Fallow parcels mauka of the community were cleared of fountain grass, ripped, and replanted as an irrigated break — food trees and native shrubs where seasonal tinder stood — slowing fire and holding storm runoff. Community workdays maintain the line, and the county's hazard-mitigation reviewers walk it each quarter. The metric that matters most here is the one that stays at zero.

records.summary: Improves the visitor experience and reduces tourism's environmental impact on the reef — pairing shoreline visitor briefings with the transect monitoring that tracks the aquatic resources visitors come to see.

location.geoContext: Nearshore waters and reef flat seaward of the parcel fabric; no TMK exists for the marine footprint. Shoreline briefing station sits at the public beach access.

records.story: Every morning the stewards set up where the trail meets the sand. Visitors get a two-minute briefing — where the reef is recovering, where to swim, why the fee they paid at the airport funds the person talking to them. The same crew runs the transect surveys the reef numbers come from. It is the program's whole thesis in one shoreline: a better visitor experience and a lighter visitor footprint, delivered person to person at the place itself.

records.summary: Improves the visitor experience and reduces tourism's environmental impact along a heavily visited trail corridor that crosses two moku — trailhead improvements, ongoing maintenance, and field-level condition reporting.

location.geoContext: Cross-moku trail corridor spanning many parcels; the footprint is the corridor easement, not a parcel set.

records.summary: Protects and restores natural resources along urban coastal lands — community restoration beds for native limu (seaweed) that rebuild aquatic resources on a heavily used shoreline.

location.geoContext: Urban shoreline reaches at the parcel–ocean boundary; restoration beds sit seaward of the parcel fabric.
